data.title: Implantica publishes Interim Report January - September 2026 (Q3)
data.description:
VADUZ, Liechtenstein, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ --

FDA approval secured and first U.S. patients treated at USC

Significant events in the third quarter of 2026

  • FDA Premarket Approval (PMA) granted for RefluxStop® on August 20, opening the world's largest medical device market and enabling a U.S. commercial launch
  • European sales grew 105% year-on-year in Q3, supported by expanding hospital adoption, including at selected centers such as Evangelisches Krankenhaus Wesel in Germany and Hospital Quirónsalud San José in Madrid
  • U.S. launch kicked off at the American Foregut Society Annual Meeting, receiving an exceptional reception from leading surgeons and gastroenterologists, with over 120 symposium attendees and nearly 30 individual meetings
  • U.S. organization significantly strengthened with highly experienced new team members, including three Regional Head of Sales Directors, a Surgical Training Lead and two clinical affairs professionals, supporting U.S. commercialization

Significant events after the end of the period

  • First RefluxStop® procedures successfully performed in the U.S. in early November by leading anti-reflux surgeon Dr. John Lipham at the University of Southern California (USC), marking a historic commercial milestone
  • European Foregut Society meeting held mid-November included a well-attended RefluxStop® symposium, where two comparative studies of RefluxStop® and fundoplication were presented, showing outcomes significantly superior with RefluxStop®
  • Training of our U.S. sales team and a handful of U.S. surgeons next in line to start with RefluxStop® completed, with the U.S. surgeon training program ongoing for additional leading U.S. surgeons

About Implantica

Implantica is a medtech company focused on bringing advanced implantable technologies into the body designed to improve patient outcomes and quality of life. The company's lead product, RefluxStop®, is an FDA approved and CE-marked implant for the treatment of gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) with the potential to transform the standard of care in anti-reflux surgery, supported by strong long-term clinical outcomes.

In addition to RefluxStop®, Implantica has developed a broad, patent-protected product pipeline partly incorporating two platform technologies: an eHealth platform designed to enable communication with and remote monitoring and control of implants inside the body, and a wireless energizing platform designed to wirelessly power implantable devices through intact skin. These investigational devices are intended to facilitate remote changes to treatment, potentially saving cost for society.

Implantica is listed on Nasdaq First North Premier Growth Market (ticker: IMP A SDB). Visit www.implantica.com for further information.

About RefluxStop®

RefluxStop® is a treatment for GERD designed to address the root cause of acid reflux. Conventional anti-reflux surgical procedures typically rely on encircling the esophagus and are often associated with side effects such as swallowing difficulties, inability to belch or vomit, and gas bloating. RefluxStop is different and aims to restore and maintain the lower esophageal sphincter in its natural anatomical position without encircling or applying pressure on the food passageway. Commercial performance from a multitude of centers supports the clinical study data collected and shows that the RefluxStop® device can successfully treat GERD without wrapping or constricting the esophageal sphincter, thereby avoiding the side effects commonly seen with the other current treatment approaches. Long-term 5-year clinical outcomes on RefluxStop® have been published in peer-reviewed scientific journals and support that a significant portion of the patient population will achieve clinically meaningful results, with minimal risks, when used in accordance with the indications for use.

Indications for Use: RefluxStop® is an implantable sterile medical device intended to treat acid and non-acid reflux in patients diagnosed with gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD). The device ensures maintenance of a normal physiological situation for the gastroesophageal junction (GEJ) in a defined intra-abdominal position, allowing natural physiological function of the lower esophageal sphincter (LES), thereby reducing or eliminating acid and non-acid reflux. The RefluxStop® Deployment Tool is indicated for patients diagnosed with Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease (GERD), defined by abnormal impedance pH and/or pH testing, and indicated for RefluxStop® implantation.

data.title: UniCredit and Germany reach broad agreement on Commerzbank takeover
data.description:
Key points:
  • Major development in two-year takeover battle
  • Merged bank's German headquarters to remain in Frankfurt as listed entity
  • Germany drops demand to name two Commerzbank supervisory board members
  • UniCredit pledges to add German nationals to its board of directors
  • Commerzbank welcomes agreement

By Holger Hansen

UniCredit and Germany have reached agreement on the big sticking points in the Italian bank's takeover of Commerzbank, a major development in the two-year battle for control of the German lender.

The agreement, laid out in a letter from UniCredit CEO Andrea Orcel to German Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil as well as a separate statement to Reuters from the German minister, states that the merged bank's German headquarters will remain in Frankfurt as a listed entity, a key German demand.

But in a concession to UniCredit, Germany has given up its insistence on naming two supervisory board members to Commerzbank .

A combination of UniCredit and Commerzbank would create a bank with more than €1.3 trillion ($1.4 trillion) in assets across two of the euro zone's ​largest economies in one of the most significant cross-border European banking deals in years.

In the letter dated November 18 and seen by Reuters, Orcel said he was "prepared to commit" to a series of binding principles and thanked Klingbeil for discussions, "which have allowed us to find common ground."

UniCredit also pledged to put German nationals on UniCredit's board of directors.

Klingbeil, in his statement to Reuters, said Germany "supports a swift process and an orderly transition of control."

"We have reached common ground and UniCredit has made clear commitments to Germany as a business location, to the rights of Commerzbank employees and to a continued constructive dialogue with the works council," Klingbeil said, referring to a body of elected employee representatives.

GERMAN GOVERNMENT STAKE

Commerzbank said in a statement it welcomed UniCredit's commitments. It said the German bank's management would "work together with UniCredit to develop a strategy that builds on the strengths of both banks."

The agreement sets the stage for a series of events, including UniCredit taking formal control, its consolidation of Commerzbank on its own balance sheet, as well as the nomination of new supervisory board members who could appoint new management.

Orcel pounced on Commerzbank in 2024, catching the lender and the government off guard by discreetly building up a holding. Commerzbank and Berlin tried to prevent the takeover, ​but gave in after UniCredit amassed a stake nearing ​50%.

Commerzbank employees have long been against a deal, in part due to Orcel's stated plans to cut jobs in Germany.

A key representative of Commerzbank's workforce said on Thursday that he welcomed the agreement for its commitment to Frankfurt as German headquarters but warned that current employee contracts remain valid.

"If those agreements are respected as announced, there may not be years of confrontation ahead," said Sascha Uebel, head of Commerzbank's works council.

"Ultimately, it is now in Andrea Orcel's hands how we, as employees, will receive him here," he told Reuters.

The German government holds a 13.3% stake in Commerzbank following a bailout during the global financial crisis.

The sale of the federal government's stake remains an open question. Orcel's letter said UniCredit's agreements "set the basis for the disposal of the government's stake", but Klingbeil's statement contains no commitment to sell.

Klingbeil ​and Orcel met in September over the Italian bank's hostile €45 billion approach. Both called the talks "constructive" but differences remained.

Since then, the European Central Bank, the European Commission and the US Federal Reserve have given a green light to a deal, clearing regulatory hurdles.

Earlier this month, Commerzbank said that it was "convinced" a deal between the two ‌banks could create value, in a markedly more bullish stance on a potential tie-up it had long resisted.

($1 = 0.9115 euros)

data.title: JD Sports cuts profit outlook again as third-quarter sales fall
data.description:
British sports and fashion retailer JD Sports cut its profit outlook for the second time in four months on Thursday after a 2.6% fall in third-quarter like-for-like sales, though trading did improve in its key North American market.

  • JD Sports forecast a year to end-January 2027 profit before tax and adjusting items of £700 million to £750 million ($919-$985 million). Its previous guidance was £700 million to £800 million

  • Prior to Thursday's update, analysts were on average forecasting £723 million. It made £852 million in 2025/26

  • Group organic sales for the 13 weeks to October 31 fell 1.1%while like-for-like sales fell 2.6%, having been down 3.1% in its second quarter

  • Like-for-like sales in the key North America market, where the group makes over a third of total sales, fell 2.2%, having been down 6.8% in the second quarter

  • Like-for-like sales fell 2.7% in Europe, 2.6% in the UK and 5.3% in Asia Pacific

  • Saw resilient sales trends in apparel and accessories, despite unseasonably warm weather delaying autumn/winter demand

  • Footwear remained soft given ongoing product cycle evolution, amidst a continued promotional market

  • Trading in Europe was affected by civil unrest, it said

  • The outcome also reflects cost-of-living pressures on JD's core young and less affluent customer base and a lack of innovation from Nike - JD's most important brand partner which is struggling to overhaul its business

  • Shares in JD are up 12% so far this year but down on a two-year basis

($1 = 0.7614 pounds)

data.title: Oil Prices Mixed as Traders Weigh Supply Outlook, Middle East Shipping Risks
data.description:
By Farhan Rafid

DOHA, Qatar--Oil prices were mixed Thursday as traders assessed the global supply outlook amid continued threats to Middle Eastern oil shipments and fresh projections for the region's energy trade.

Front-month Brent crude futures rose 0.3% to $92.25 a barrel, while front-month West Texas Intermediate crude futures slipped 0.1% to $83.21 a barrel.

U.S. commercial crude inventories rose by 3.4 million barrels to 417.8 million barrels last week, according to data released Wednesday by the Energy Information Administration. The increase exceeded the 1-million-barrel build expected by analysts surveyed by The Wall Street Journal.

Meanwhile, the International Energy Agency said Thursday that prolonged disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz could substantially reduce the world's reliance on the waterway over the next decade as Middle Eastern producers develop alternative export routes.

In its World Energy Outlook, the agency said oil flows through the strait could decline from around 20 million barrels a day before the conflict to 8.5 million barrels a day by 2030 and fewer than 2 million by 2035 under a scenario in which severe shipping disruptions persist.

The agency said the Middle East would remain the world's largest oil-exporting region even under that scenario, as investment in new pipelines and alternative supply routes helps producers maintain access to international markets.

The IEA expects the global oil market to record a surplus of around 1.7 million barrels a day in the fourth quarter, widening to approximately 3.8 million barrels a day next year as Middle Eastern production recovers faster than demand.

The outlook comes amid continued security threats to regional oil infrastructure and shipping, which have complicated efforts to restore exports through the Strait of Hormuz.

Analysts at Sparta Commodities said Wednesday that recovering Middle Eastern supplies remained vulnerable to attacks on vessels and energy infrastructure. They also pointed to disruptions at Russian refineries, which have increased crude availability for export while keeping European diesel supplies tight.

Meanwhile, Scott Shelton, an energy specialist at TP ICAP, a London-based interdealer broker, pointed to a stronger U.S. dollar and weakness across commodity markets as additional factors in crude trading, alongside expectations of a substantial global supply build next year.

Write to Farhan Rafid at farhan.rafid@wsj.com

data.title: Before the bell: European futures rise led by AI complex
data.description:
Key points:
  • EuroSTOXX50 futures up 0.7%
  • Anthropic debuts on Nasdaq
  • Nasdaq futures rise

BEFORE THE BELL: EUROPEAN FUTURES RISE LED BY AI COMPLEX

European shares were set to open higher on Thursday after suffering their biggest two-day slide since March, with the AI complex driving premarket gains as investors cheered Anthropic's upsized IPO, priced above its initial range ahead of its Nasdaq debut later in the day.

Nasdaq futures rallied 2% after Wednesday's modest gains, while chip stocks and other AI-related plays in Europe, including ASML , Infineon and Siemens Energy , featured among the top gainers premarket. Shares in Soitec were called 10% higher after the French semiconductor materials supplier beat earnings expectations.

Futures on the euro zone's blue-chip EuroSTOXX50 index rose 0.7%, while contracts on Germany's DAX (GDAXI) and the UK's FTSE 100 CURRENCYCOM:UK100 added 0.3% and 0.1%, respectively. Shares in Commerzbank gained 0.8% on Tradegate after UniCredit and Germany reached agreement on key sticking points in the Italian lender's takeover.

Steadying crude oil prices and a bounce from seven-month lows in London copper futures may also offer some reprieve to commodity stocks following this week's battering.

In Asia, however, tech sentiment was clouded after Tencent's quarterly revenue growth slowed more than expected, sending the stock to their lowest in over two years. The Chinese tech giant said new US chip curbs would likely slow development of its next AI model. Amsterdam-listed Prosus , Tencent's largest shareholder, fell 2.6% on Tradegate.

data.description: Eurozone government bond yields fall in opening trade, shrugging off interest-rate hike expectations and heavy bond supply on Thursday. data.title: UK's Sage to cut management layers in £100 million restructuring
data.description:
Sage , a British supplier of software for small and medium-sized businesses, said it would cut its management to help drive growth after it met market expectations with a 13% rise in full-year operating profit on Thursday

  • Chief Executive Steve Hare said: "Sage achieved an excellent performance in FY26, with double-digit revenue growth, continued margin expansion and robust cash flows."

  • The company said it would reduce management layers and consolidate its technology capabilities, resulting in a restructuring charge of around £100 million this year

  • "We expect these actions to create a faster and more agile business, driving growth and enhancing operating leverage," it said

  • For the year to end-September, underlying revenue rose 10% to £2.78 billion, while annualised recurring revenue was up 11% at £2.88 billion. Underlying operating profit rose 13% to £681 million

  • The company increased its margin by 0.7 percentage points to 24.5%

  • It said it expected organic total revenue growth this year to be in the region of 10% and underlying operating margins were expected to continue trending upwards
